evidence.summary: Task phases and cooperative cancellation exist; bounded TaskScope cancels pending tasks and observes cancellation between calls.
verification_resource_transition returns CancelStale, cleanup obligation, and Unknown evidence for superseded in-flight work.
The owned process group stopped 52 ms after N+1 publication; N did not establish current PASS and N+1 proceeded.
process_run is synchronous and exposes no source-visible handle to interrupt the active provider/effect.
The 30-second fixture timed out without readable OOM or cgroup cleanup counters; no repeated larger probe was run.

metadata.pressure_boundary: synchronous external effect cannot be interrupted by source-visible runtime cancellation

reproduction.instructions: Inspect mncs.std.task.v1 and scope.v1, mncs-embed TaskScope, then run tests/test_continuous.py::test_superseding_generation_cancels_owned_process_group. The remaining runtime effect-handle gap is reproduced by MNCS-LANG-64AD712CD2DE.

summary: Task and structured-scope cancellation are available, and Forge native semantics now classify superseded work and request cancellation. A generic Forge Runner can terminate the owned process group in 52 ms and report cleanup facts. However, source-visible cooperative cancellation still cannot interrupt a task already blocked inside synchronous process_run; cgroup-zero cleanup was not proven.

workaround.description: Forge Runner realizes native cancellation decisions by signaling and reaping the owned process group/cgroup where available.
